title: Edit Decisions
description: Editorial decisions produced by the Edit Agent.

cuts._why_source_is_not_required: THE NAME OF THIS KEY IS HISTORICAL: `source` IS required now. It is kept because the name is the question that was asked, and the value is the answer that reversed it. THIS CHANGED TWICE AND THE SECOND CHANGE REVERSED THE FIRST. `source` was originally required because every pipeline that had exercised this schema cut from footage. On 2026-11-07 the king-tut run - the first to CHECKPOINT the edit stage - made it OPTIONAL, because an authored cut has no source file: it names a component and DRAWS its picture, and the narrated-documentary films run 60% of their cuts that way. On 2026-11-09 it was made REQUIRED AGAIN, with a different meaning: every cut must say what it is a cut OF, and for an authored cut that is the SLOT ID from scene_plan.json rather than a file path. An id is not a path and has no suffix - see tests/automation/test_authored_cut_shape.py. The first reasoning was right that there is no FILE; it was wrong that there is therefore nothing to name.
cuts._why_additional_properties: THE NAME OF THIS KEY IS HISTORICAL TOO: `additionalProperties` on the cut is now false. ALSO CHANGED TWICE, AND THE REASONING SURVIVED THE CHANGE. Component props ARE open-ended - a schematic's layers, a timeline's events, a map_route's markers - and they are NOT unchecked: lib/buildability.py validates every one against remotion-composer/component-contract.json, which is stricter than an enumeration here could be, because it checks required props, required keys on every array item, and enum ranges PER COMPONENT. Enumerating them a second time in this file would be a copy that drifts. That is why this schema still does not list them. What changed on 2026-11-09 is WHERE they sit. They used to sit FLAT beside `type`, which forced `additionalProperties: true` on the whole cut - so the open set was the entire cut object, and a typo in an EDITORIAL field passed validation silently. Now they sit under the single `scene` key, which is open, and the cut around it is CLOSED. lib/build_render_props.py flattens `scene` onto the cut before the renderer sees it, so the shape remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx reads is unchanged. One open key instead of one open object, and the checking stays where it already was.
cuts._found_by: The king-tut run, which is the first to CHECKPOINT the edit stage. Two delivered films carried authored cuts past this schema without it ever being applied to them. The `scene` sub-object came from noah, authored under it: all 159 cuts validate clean. The four films published before 2026-11-09 are NOT migrated - they load, and the flattening is safe on all of them.

source.description: What this is a cut OF. For a SOURCED cut: a source file path or asset-manifest ID. For an AUTHORED cut: the SLOT ID from scene_plan.json - an id, not a path, so it has no file suffix. Required either way; see `_why_source_carries_the_slot_id`.

animation.description: Motion applied to still images (e.g. ken-burns-slow-zoom, pan-left, static)

transition_in.description: Transition type entering this cut (e.g. fade, dissolve, cut, wipe)

backgroundColor.description: Backing color used behind this cut by composition runtimes

beat.description: The beat type of the narration this cut sits under. The planner takes the shot-length band from it; lib/verify_rhythm.py checks the cut against that band.

register.description: The emotional register of the narration this cut sits under, from the script. With the beat it selects the row in the playbook's mood table.

asset_class.description: CLIP zero-shot class of the asset on screen. It vetoes the mood table in one direction: a push into a dense frame becomes a lock.

hold_multiplier.description: Scales the beat's hold band; it does not replace it.

internal_motion.description: Whether the shot moves inside the frame. A reveal may only hold past the stills cap when this is true — otherwise a long hold is a slideshow with a beat label on it.

camera.description: Camera intent for this shot. The move is chosen from the beat and the asset, and the reason is recorded so an edit can be read back.

ramp.description: the act's one speed ramp into a hard cut

audio_lead_frames.description: Positive: this scene's audio leads its picture by N frames (J-cut). Negative: the picture leads the narration (L-cut). Zero or absent: a straight cut.

scene.description: Scene payload for a hand-authored cut, used when composition_mode is atelier. The cut object proper is a closed set of EDITORIAL decisions — where the boundary is, how the camera moves, whether the sound leads it. An authored scene also needs a component name and its props, which are a different kind of thing and vary per component, so they live here. lib/build_render_props.py flattens this onto the cut before the renderer sees it.

audio.description: Audio configuration for narration, music, and SFX.

source.description: Path to subtitle file or asset ID

color.description: Primary text color (hex or ASS format)

music.description: Legacy top-level music config. Prefer audio.music for new pipelines.

transitions.description: Global transition list. Per-cut transitions in cuts[].transition_in/out are preferred.

renderer_family.description: Locked at proposal stage — creative grammar for this deliverable. Preserved from proposal_packet; edit MUST NOT change without a logged decision.

render_runtime.description: Locked at proposal stage — technical runtime that realizes renderer_family. Edit MUST carry this forward unchanged unless a logged render_runtime_selection decision overrides it.

composition_mode.description: Locked at proposal — HOW the composition is built. Edit MUST carry forward unchanged. 'atelier' routes video_compose to _render_via_atelier (no cut-schema, no stock registry); requires `bespoke` block below.

bespoke.description: Required when composition_mode='atelier'. Contract for the hand-authored, project-local Remotion render. See tools/video/video_compose.py → _render_via_atelier docstring.

entry.description: Path to the project-local Remotion entry .tsx (typically projects/<slug>/index.tsx). If outside remotion-composer/, auto-staged via directory junction/symlink at render time.

composition_id.description: id registered in that entry's Root

art_direction.description: Short commitment to a fresh visual language (or a path to art-direction.md). REQUIRED — enforced by _run_atelier_checks.

props_path.description: Absolute path to a props JSON (Remotion --props)

public_dir.description: Per-project public dir (avoids copying the bloated shared remotion-composer/public/)

total_duration_seconds.description: The finished timeline's length. REQUIRED BY pipeline_defs/narrated-documentary.yaml, whose edit stage lists 'total_duration_seconds matches the sum of cut durations' as a success criterion and 'Timeline duration within 10% of the script duration' beside it - and both delivered films carry it. It was absent from this schema, which forbids unknown top-level keys, so the one artifact the manifest asks to be checked could not be written as a checkpoint at all.
